iOS 27 beta 5 was released this week, confirming a feature Apple had previously hinted at: paying to upgrade to a higher-tier iCloud+ plan, which unlocks more Apple Intelligence capabilities.

Upgrading your iCloud+ plan unlocks more AI features in iOS 27

If you already subscribe to iCloud+ or Apple One, subscribing to iOS 27 will bring new features.

You'll get more usage-limited Apple Intelligence features (such as image generation), as well as new HomeKit Secure Video capabilities for your cameras.

But based on what's seen in iOS 27 beta 5, the limits for these new features appear to vary depending on which iCloud+ plan you subscribe to.

Within the Home app → Home Settings → Apple Intelligence → Cameras & Language, iOS 27 now displays how many of your cameras are supported for AI summaries under your iCloud+ plan. Quoting a post by Stephen Robles on X:

The image on the right shared by Robles shows a new screen that appears after tapping "View iCloud+ plans" from the Cameras & Language page. It reads:

Upgrade your iCloud+ plan for more Apple Intelligence features. Get more smart capabilities, more storage, and more.

The page shows your current plan and offers the option to upgrade to a higher tier. It doesn't yet display all the different plans, which is likely a minor issue with the beta version and will be resolved before the official release.

From what I've currently seen in the beta version, the 2TB iCloud+ plan appears to provide AI summaries for 5 cameras, while the 12TB plan goes up to 15. What other plans offer is not yet clear.

But based on the wording of this new upgrade page in the beta version, it's almost certain that each higher tier of iCloud+ plan will not only support AI summaries for more cameras, but also increase the usage allowance for other AI features.

This is also consistent with what CEO Tim Cook said on Apple's last earnings call.

What are your thoughts on Apple tying AI feature limits to iCloud+ plans? Let us know in the comments.
